decision: Airflow orchestration for daily warehouse exports
version: Apache Airflow 3.3.2, latest stable verified against the Apache distribution index on deployment day
decisions: LocalExecutor with one active task globally, one-slot export_jobs pool and one active run per DAG; no Celery, Redis or additional RabbitMQ use.
Separate API, scheduler and DAG processor containers; a dedicated airflow_meta database and restricted owner role on the existing PostgreSQL 18 cluster.
Two daily full exports at 06:00 and 06:15 America/Toronto; catchup disabled; these initial lab schedules are project defaults.
Existing exporter and S3-only validator run as bounded, detached one-off containers. No Docker socket or business database/storage/broker credentials are mounted into Airflow.
A pinned-host-key SSH identity reaches a root-owned forced command. Its strict JSON allowlist permits dependency checks, the two existing export/validation jobs and invoice receipt checks only.
A request identity derives from dataset and Airflow DAG-run ID, never task attempt. The root journal survives task/SSH loss and reuses completed publications.
Invoice completion requires the application's durable delivery ledger to match publication, manifest hash, row hash and row count. Orders retain direct S3 consumption.
Readiness means healthy services and a recent successful warehouse scan; it does not certify a contiguous CDC watermark or source transaction boundary. No purge operation is exposed.
File-mounted generated secrets, FAB authentication, loopback UI publishing through SSH/IAP, persistent metadata and task logs.
Metadata initialization uses a five-connection pool; runtime components use two connections with no overflow. Initial schema creation holds multiple connections and cannot use a two-connection pool.
limitations: Single VM, shared PostgreSQL instance and local disk; no HA or off-VM disaster recovery.
Airflow DAG authors remain trusted operators; restricted job submission is an additional boundary, not hostile-tenant isolation.
A failed Airflow task may leave a detached job running. Recover with the same request identity; do not delete journals or create a new run merely to resume.
Two retries after an initial failure; exhausted retries appear in the UI. External notifications and escalation routing are not configured.
Persistent task logs, job journals and exports require a future reviewed retention policy; no automatic evidence deletion.
Daily full snapshots are for this lab's measured volume. Incremental export contracts and Spark require separate measurement and design.
Application cutover, SQL-object migration, safe source CDC cleanup and decommissioning remain separate unfinished workstreams.
